newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque leader found hanged hours before court date.
newsitem.headline: Basque leader found hanged hours before court date.

text.p: A leader of ETA's political arm Herri Batasuna (HB) was found hanged at his family home in northern Spain on Monday only hours before he was due to appear before the Supreme Court, police said.
The body of Eugenio Aranburu, 41, was found at 1 p.m. (1200 GMT), but Basque police could not confirm whether it was suicide. They said they were still investigating the cause of death.

Aranburu was due to appear in Spain's Supreme Court at 5 p.m. to answer charges he and other HB leaders promoted violence. HB sources said they had been planning to meet at his house at that time to discuss how to handle the summons.
Five members of HB's 25-person leadership were sent to prison last week for failing to appear before the Supreme Court, which has summoned all of them.
On Saturday, HB members held a news conference urging demonstrations and strikes to protest at the jailings.

HB, which does not renounce violence as a means of achieving Basque independence, is to be charged with distributing a videotape that promotes the violent separatist rebel group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) and for justifying two murders.
ETA, which has murdered some 800 people since starting its drive for independence in 1968, was blamed for a car bomb earlier on Monday that killed one man.
